success_patterns: Four of the eight answers (Gadsden Purchase, I Remember Mama, Jamestown, Bumpkin) came from an archive/flashcard passage that repeated the clue nearly verbatim, with the answer attached. Rule 3 already covers this.

Bare definition or etymology clues with no 'this' ('A short, witty saying'; 'From the Middle Dutch for "little barrel", it's another way of saying yokel') were solved by finding the dictionary headword that the passages gloss with the clue's words. The answer was one plain word (epigram, bumpkin).

A full quoted line of verse with no blank and no 'this' ('I think that I shall never see a poem lovely as a tree') asked for the author. Every passage paired the line with 'Poem by Joyce Kilmer', so the answer was the author's name, not the poem title.

'This <noun>' clues (play, author, settlement) were answered with an entity of exactly that noun's type, taken from the passages that tied it to the clue's distinctive details (the children's names, the 500 to 60 settlers).
Set-completion clues ('Brahma, Shiva & this one') were answered with the missing member. The answer was not a clue name, and no descriptor was added.

patch.reasoning: Most successes already follow existing rules (Rule 3 verbatim archive hits, type matching, missing-member sets). Two patterns are only partly covered. First, bare definition and etymology clues with no 'Term for' wording (the answer is a headword, usually one word, written as the dictionary shows it). Second, a complete quoted line of verse or speech with no blank (the answer is the author or speaker, as in 'Poem by X', not the title). Both are small, targeted additions that need no mandatory line, and they avoid the over-broad edits that were rejected earlier.

edits.target: - 'N-word' hints ('this 3-word phrase') work like a letter count: the answer must have exactly N words.
edits.content: - BARE DEFINITION / ETYMOLOGY clues with no 'this' and no 'Term for' ('A short, witty saying'; 'From the Middle Dutch for "little barrel", it's another way of saying yokel'): the answer is the single word being defined. Find the dictionary, thesaurus or crossword passage whose headword is glossed with the clue's own words ('epigram - a witty saying'; 'bumpkin ... < Middle Dutch bommekijn little barrel'). Answer with that headword as a plain singular word. Do not answer with a longer phrase, an example of the thing, or a synonym that only fits part of the clue.

edits.target: - 'N-word' hints ('this 3-word phrase') work like a letter count: the answer must have exactly N words.
edits.content: - A FULL QUOTED LINE (verse, lyric, speech) with no '...' blank and no 'this <work>' asks for its AUTHOR or SPEAKER. Passages pair the line with headings like 'Trees by Joyce Kilmer' or 'Poem by X'. Answer the person's name ('Joyce Kilmer'), not the poem title or a word from the line. If the clue has '...' or says 'this poem/song', the slot is the missing words or the title instead.
